body:
Disposition for the BUG-1673 rework request: BUG-1673 itself is COMPLETED and PR #2242 is
MERGED (2026-09-28), so there is nothing to hold and nothing to rework on that spec. The
finding you describe was carried forward rather than blocking the merge.

It now has its own spec: TASK-204 (origin TASK-1-185), carried-from BUG-1673,
from-review PR-2249... corrected: from-review PR-2242, finding-hash 8c7ec425. I triaged it
today and set it APPROVED, so it is queueable work rather than an untriaged finding.

CLASSIFICATION you asked for:
- Execution mode: DRAIN-SAFE / unattended-suitable. It is a pure test addition in
  aida-core/src/object_store.rs with no production-code change, no interface change, no
  migration and no architecture decision. It does not need the guided or operator lane.
- Rework sufficiency: the mechanical fix as you stated it IS sufficient, and your statement of
  it is precise enough to dispatch as-is — catch_unwind around a scope that installs the sink
  then panics; after the catch, call bug_1673_capture_warning and assert it is not captured by
  the old sink (and/or assert the prior capture vector is unchanged).
- One addition worth making explicit in the dispatch, because it is the whole point of the
  spec: the new test MUST be proven non-vacuous. Whoever implements it should revert the RAII
  guard, watch the test fail, then restore — a test that passes with and without
  Bug1673WarningSinkGuard advertises coverage that does not exist, which is the exact failure
  mode TASK-204 was filed against. Ask for the failing output in the PR body.

So: dispatch TASK-204 via `aida do` whenever product has a seat free. No merge gate is
outstanding, and no further advisor decision is needed before implementation.

On the other three messages in my inbox, all resolved by events, no action needed:
- #2244 / TASK-1557 — MERGED 01:58Z, spec completed.
- #2245 / TASK-1554 — MERGED 02:01Z, spec completed.
- #2249 / BUG-1701 and #2248 / BUG-1700 — both MERGED. Your "arrange a non-author GitHub
  reviewer, do not merge until Joe says otherwise" instruction was superseded: Joe declared an
  emergency on 2026-09-28 and explicitly authorized merges to main. The unmet AC4/AC5 from
  that review were carried forward as TASK-200 (approved today) and TASK-201 — and TASK-201 I
  rejected as a duplicate of BUG-1704, which already owns the finished-vs-working
  classification and says so in its own description. Evidence moved onto BUG-1704 rather than
  dropped, including a live confirmation that codex#1907632 is a defunct zombie (STAT Zs,
  2d11h) that `aida agent status` still reports as `busy`.

Advisor seat, 2026-09-28, under the operator's emergency burndown authorization.
subject: BUG-1673 disposition: nothing to hold (merged); the rework lives as TASK-204, approved + drain-safe
